What is your system VRAM usage?

I can bet that you're running over the 4GB frame buffer with both the Editor and the Game running, and Vulkan Doesn't take it nicely. Switch to DX12 and that'll work significantly better.

if this is indeed it it's a duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102644 which is itself related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/95254

I've seen similar issues with any project that has:
- a 3d camera
- a mesh instance visible by the camera
- a world environment
- a directional light
... and was also launched from the terminal, like so: `godot path/to/project.godot`. Note that unlike the OP, I don't have the editor GUI running, but the issue still persists.

There are occasional freezes every few seconds. Nothing is wrong when the game is exported, so I guess it's not *that* big of a deal. Just immensely annoying for development.

yea with 6gb it's not like an empty scene would be able to eat that away... as for the terminal yea it's always a possibility that it's allocating memory when it shouldn't which would itself be a bug.. so what you're having is definitely not a VRAM issue.

Still would be helpful knowing more about the system, like OS, GPU, GPU driver.

I haven't been able to reproduce this on an AMD Radeon RX 6600 so There is a possibility this issue is an Nvidia driver issue (especially given the post Blackwell drivers being a disaster after disaster), Now my assumption is you're running Windows, with a GTX 1060 6gb, or less likely a 2060 or 1660 or even less likely a 3050 6gb. If it's the 1060 it could also be a driver issue specific to Pascal, but more testing is required.

This freeze-every-second issue happens when your graphics card runs out of VRAM. Check the VRAM resource profiler to make sure there's no 4K textures using a lot of VRAM or similar. Also, If you happen to be using the VoxelGI node, this will increase your VRAM usage a lot without showing anything in the VRAM resource profiler.

I managed to find another way to cause these freezes besides running out of VRAM (and fix it in my own game).

It goes something as follows (I'm still figuring it out, in an attempt to make a 
- allocate a bunch of VRAM with textures or meshes rendered on the screen (0.5 GB in my case)
- cause the `process` to get stuck for a few seconds (10 seems to be enough), by either sleeping on it or doing enough calculations that some `process` tick lasts very long
- on the same frame, reallocate that vram by removing the rendered nodes and allocating new ones (with new textures and meshes that weren't previously rendered)
- from now on, the project will experience periodic freezes, around once every 1-3 seconds (notably, these freezes show up in the profiler as `process` taking up way more time than usual, even if the calculations inside of that `process` tick take very little time)

To fix it (in my project), I distributed calculations over multiple frames so that no `process` tick stalls the main thread for too long.
Note that in my case this *wasn't* a VRAM issue, in spite of having the same symptomps as the OP. My GPU has 6 GB of VRAM and I made sure to keep it low while doing the tests.
